text: Ich bin bei Stress weniger hektisch und überlege erst, bevor ich handle. Mein Team auf der Arbeit hat das schon bemerkt und meinte, ich sei viel entspannter geworden.
Its hard to explain but I just dont get as worked up anymore. Stuff happens, I deal with it, move on. Before I would ruminate for days on every little thing someone said to me.

The experience showed me that I've been living with a constant low level of fear since my childhood, and that most of my stress reactions are really about that old fear. My dad was unpredictable and sometimes violent. I learned to be on guard all the time. During the experience I felt for the first time what it's like to be completely safe, and it made me cry for an hour. Now, when I'm stressed, I can sometimes remember that feeling of safety and tell my body that it's okay. I've also started trauma therapy, which is helping me work through this in a more structured way.
Weiß ich nicht genau. Vielleicht ein bisschen ruhiger, aber ich bin nicht sicher, ob das an der Erfahrung liegt.
I see challenges more as opportunities to grow. When my startup failed last year, I was disappointed, but I also saw it as a learning experience and I started again pretty quickly.
Less panicky when stuff goes wrong

Ich habe gelernt, auch in schwierigen Zeiten bei mir zu bleiben und meine Gefühle wahrzunehmen, ohne von ihnen überwältigt zu werden. In der Erfahrung kamen sehr starke Gefühle von Angst und Trauer hoch, und ich habe gemerkt, dass ich sie aushalten kann, wenn ich einfach atme und sie da sein lasse. Das übe ich jetzt im Alltag. Als meine Oma letztes Jahr gestorben ist, war ich sehr traurig, aber ich konnte die Trauer zulassen und bin nicht wie früher in ein tiefes Loch gefallen.

I think I'm better at dealing with stressful events because I'm more honest with myself about how I feel. I used to say I'm fine when I wasn't, and then I'd crash. Now I admit when something is hard, to myself and to others.

The experience took place at a festival and it was mostly fun, with friends, dancing and music. I don't think it had a big influence on how I handle stress. Maybe I learned that I can enjoy life more, but stress-wise, it's the same.
Ich gehe mit Konflikten offener um und spreche Probleme schneller an, statt sie in mich hineinzufressen. Das hat vor allem meine Beziehung entspannt.

I feel that I've become more resilient. I lost my job during the pandemic and had to move back in with my parents, which was really hard for my ego. But I somehow trusted that it was a phase. I took it one day at a time, I helped my parents around the house, I went for walks in the forest every morning, and I started a small online business that now pays my bills. Before the experience I think I would have sunk into depression.

It made it worse at first. I felt very fragile for a few months after the experience and couldn't handle any stress at all. I'd get panic attacks at work. It's a lot better now, I would say I'm back to normal, maybe even a little calmer than before, but that first period was rough.
Probleme erscheinen mir kleiner, weil ich mich als Teil von etwas Größerem fühle.
I don't take on other people's stress so much anymore. I'm a very empathic person and I used to absorb everyone's problems. Now I can be there for them without carrying it home.

Ever since the experience I have been noticing my thoughts more, especially the negative ones. When I'm stressed I tend to think the worst, that I'll be fired, that my partner will leave me, that I'm going to get sick. I now see these as thoughts and not facts, and I can talk back to them. I learned this partly in the experience, where I saw my mind creating all kinds of scary stories, and partly from reading about CBT afterwards. It has made stressful events much easier to deal with.
Ich mache mir weniger Sorgen und kann Belastungen leichter wegstecken.
Same as before, didn't notice anything.

I'm a police officer, and I've seen a lot of terrible things. I had been struggling with intrusive images and irritability for years. The experience was part of a retreat for first responders. What it gave me was a sense of compassion for myself and for the people I meet on the job, including the ones who do bad things. I saw that most of them are hurting too. That has changed how I handle stressful calls. I'm calmer, less reactive, and I don't carry so much anger home with me. I also talk to my colleagues about what we see, which we never used to do. We've started a small peer group.
Seitdem gehe ich in stressigen Phasen regelmäßig joggen und meditiere abends zehn Minuten. Das hilft mir enorm.
I trust myself more to get through hard times. I've been through the hardest night of my life during that trip and I made it.
It made me less afraid of uncertainty. I used to need to know everything in advance, and stress came from not knowing. Now I'm better at living with not knowing and I take things as they come.

Ich habe gemerkt, dass ich in Stresssituationen immer sofort an mir selbst zweifle und denke, dass ich etwas falsch gemacht habe. Das versuche ich jetzt bewusst zu bemerken und zu hinterfragen. Oft hilft es, mit einer Freundin darüber zu reden, die mir dann sagt, dass ich zu streng mit mir bin.
I'm much better at saying no and setting boundaries, which means I have fewer stressful situations in the first place.

I feel more able to cope with stressful things. When I had a car accident last spring I stayed surprisingly calm, I called the police and my insurance, and I didn't have nightmares afterwards like I did after my last accident years ago.

Die Erfahrung hat mir gezeigt, dass ich viel stärker bin, als ich dachte. Ich habe während des Trips eine sehr schwierige Phase durchgestanden, in der ich große Angst hatte und dachte, ich würde nie wieder normal werden. Als es vorbei war, hatte ich das Gefühl, dass mich nichts mehr so leicht umhauen kann. Diese Zuversicht begleitet mich seitdem. Wenn heute etwas Belastendes passiert, sage ich mir: Du hast schon Schlimmeres überstanden. Das klingt einfach, hilft mir aber sehr. Ich bin auch geduldiger mit mir selbst geworden, wenn ich mal nicht so gut funktioniere.
I used to be a perfectionist and every mistake was a disaster. Now I can laugh about my mistakes and learn from them.
I'm better at handling the stress of my studies. I see the bigger picture now, that grades aren't everything, and I take more breaks. I also talk to my study group when I'm overwhelmed.
Keine größeren Veränderungen. Ich gehe mit Stress so um wie immer.

Since the experience I've been dealing with stress in a much healthier way. I used to binge eat when I was stressed, sometimes several times a week. During the experience I saw very clearly that I eat to fill an emptiness, a loneliness that I've carried since I was a teenager. That was really painful to see, but it also made sense of everything. I've since joined an eating disorder support group and I see a therapist. When I feel stressed now, I try to pause and ask what I really need. Sometimes it's a call with a friend, sometimes it's a bath, sometimes it's just crying. I still binge sometimes, but much less often, and I'm kinder to myself when it happens.
I think I'm more patient and less reactive overall

Ich sehe Schwierigkeiten heute eher als Herausforderungen, an denen ich wachsen kann, und nicht mehr als Bedrohung. Das hat meinen Umgang mit Stress sehr verändert. Ich gehe Probleme aktiver an und lasse mich nicht mehr so schnell entmutigen.
Better at accepting stuff that's out of my control

I have more empathy for people who stress me out. My boss for example, I used to see him as a tyrant, but during the experience I saw him as a scared little man under a lot of pressure. That makes it easier to deal with him without taking it personally.
Ich bin entspannter, wenn es um Termine und Fristen geht. Früher habe ich mich verrückt gemacht, heute mache ich einfach einen Schritt nach dem anderen.
The experience helped me to stop catastrophizing. I'm better at handling stress because I can see what's actually happening instead of what my mind thinks might happen.

Before the experience, my reaction to stress was to drink and smoke. I'd come home from work and have a few beers and a joint just to switch off. During the experience I saw how I was numbing myself, and that the stress was still there underneath, just pushed away. I've since cut down on both, and I go to the gym or play guitar instead. It's harder in the moment because I actually have to feel the stress, but in the long run I feel much better and I deal with problems instead of avoiding them.

Ich kann mit belastenden Ereignissen inzwischen viel besser umgehen, weil ich gelernt habe, nicht sofort zu bewerten. Ich nehme erst einmal wahr, was passiert, und reagiere dann. Das gibt mir viel mehr Handlungsspielraum.
In stressful situations I'm calmer and more focused. I can think clearly instead of freezing up.

I've been taking care of my wife since her stroke two years ago, and that's a constant source of stress. The experience happened before that, but I think it prepared me. It taught me that love is the most important thing, and that I can handle a lot if I stay connected to that. On the hard days, I remind myself why I'm doing this. I also learned to ask for help from our kids and from a support group for caregivers.
Ich bin mir nicht sicher, ob sich etwas verändert hat. Ich glaube eher nicht.
